discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new time-reversal-invariant electronic phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a Z2 topological invariant, with protected helical edge states. This insight generalised the topological classification of matter beyond the integer quantum Hall effect and without magnetic fields. In 2007 Molenkamp's group, working with HgTe/CdTe quantum wells grown with exceptional care, observed quantised edge conductance near 2e^2/h and its dependence on well thickness. This was the first experimental realisation of a two-dimensional topological insulator, and it was later confirmed by nonlocal transport. These works launched the field of topological insulators, which was soon extended to three dimensions. They underpin the quantum anomalous Hall effect, axion insulators, and proposals for topological superconductivity and fault-tolerant quantum devices. They are a model of close dialogue between theory and experiment, with precise quantisation revealing new physics.
